area: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/notes/{id} and /notes/{id}/export (FE /notes/[id])
hypothesis: Note read/export enforces only workspace_id + require_viewer with NO project-visibility check. A note attached to a private/draft project is fully readable/exportable by any workspace viewer/member who is NOT a ProjectMember — unlike Project detail which DOES enforce visibility (projects/service.py get_project). This is a visibility-residue IDOR variation not covered by T1-T18 (which test project/RAG visibility, not the note/meeting read surface).
repro_steps: 1) owner d@e.com: create a project, set visibility=private (do NOT add a@e.com as ProjectMember). 2) owner creates a Note inside that private project with sensitive text. 3) Confirm member a@e.com (role member) canNOT see the project on /projects (visibility filter hides it). 4) As a@e.com, capture/guess the note id (e.g. from owner's earlier shared link, or list /notes which has no visibility filter) and navigate to /notes/<id>, then call GET .../notes/<id>/export?format=md. Observe whether full private note content is returned (200 with body) instead of 404.
expected: Member who is not a ProjectMember of the private/draft project should get 404 on both note GET and export, mirroring project-level visibility enforcement.
suspected_defect: 200 + full private note body/markdown leaks to non-member; cross-member confidential content disclosure.
grounding: backend/src/notes/service.py:137-144 (get_note: only workspace_id), :184-207 (export_note: no visibility), notes/router.py:44-70 (require_viewer only); contrast projects/service.py:136-159 which enforces draft/private. notes/repository.py find_by_id filters only workspace_id.

area: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/meetings/{id} and /meetings/{id}/export (FE /meetings/[id])
hypothesis: Same visibility-residue as SENTINEL-01 but for meetings: get_meeting_detail / export_meeting only check workspace_id + require_viewer. A meeting linked only to a private project (or whose transcript is sensitive) is readable/exportable by any viewer regardless of ProjectMember mapping. area: DELETE /members/{id} then re-invite — orphan ProjectMember residue (private-project RAG visibility)
hypothesis: Removing a WorkspaceMember (invite_service.remove_member -> repository.remove_member) deletes ONLY the workspace_members row; it does NOT delete the user's ProjectMember rows (no DB cascade, no app cleanup). The RAG/visibility private-project check (_visibility_filter_sql) only verifies project_members.user_id, with no WorkspaceMember join. So if the removed user is later re-invited as a plain member, the stale ProjectMember row silently re-grants access to a private project they were never re-added to.
repro_steps: 1) owner d@e.com adds a@e.com as ProjectMember of a PRIVATE project P. 2) owner removes a@e.com from the workspace (Members tab -> remove). 3) owner re-invites a@e.com via a fresh invite link (role=member) and a@e.com accepts. 4) As a@e.com, open /projects (does P appear?) and run RAG ask on the workspace; check whether chunks from private project P surface, and whether GET /projects/P returns 200. Owner never re-added a@e.com to P.
expected: After workspace removal, the user's ProjectMember rows should be revoked. On re-invite as member, they must NOT regain private-project P access until explicitly re-added as ProjectMember.
suspected_defect: Stale ProjectMember row resurrects private-project visibility (project visible, RAG returns private chunks) without re-authorization.
grounding: backend/src/workspaces/repository.py:130-139 remove_member deletes only WorkspaceMember; invite_service.py:261-280 remove_member has no ProjectMember cleanup; projects/models.py:54-78 ProjectMember has FK to projects/workspaces but no ON DELETE from workspace_members; embeddings/repository.py:166-183 _visibility_filter_sql private branch only checks project_members.user_id.

area: Semantic cache visibility residue after project visibility flip (public -> private)
hypothesis: SemanticCache stores a max_visibility snapshot at write time; find_similar_cache uses max_visibility=='public' as a fast-path that SKIPS the per-chunk _all_chunks_visible re-check for non-admins. If a project's visibility is changed public->private AFTER a cache entry was created (TTL 7d), the cached row keeps max_visibility='public' and a non-member member will still be served the cached answer containing now-private content.
repro_steps: 1) owner d@e.com: create project P visibility=public with a note containing a distinctive secret phrase; wait for embedding. 2) member a@e.com (not ProjectMember): RAG ask a question that hits P's content so a cache entry is written (done event cached:false, then re-ask to confirm cached:true). 3) owner PATCHes P visibility to private (does NOT delete caches). 4) a@e.com re-asks the SAME question within 7d. Observe whether the cached answer + sources containing the secret phrase are still returned (search_results event chunks).
expected: Visibility change to private should invalidate or bypass the stale public-marked cache; non-member must not receive the now-private cached content.
suspected_defect: cache fast-path serves stale public-marked answer/sources after the underlying project became private — visibility downgrade not propagated to SemanticCache.max_visibility.
grounding: backend/src/embeddings/repository.py:376-385 (is_admin/max_vis fast-path skips _all_chunks_visible when max_vis=='public'); compute_max_visibility:393-423 snapshots at store; projects update_project (service.py:239-268) changes visibility with NO delete_caches call; rag/service.py:202-223 stores max_vis once.

area: RAG citation [N] -> SourceViewer mapping (FE /search)
hypothesis: Citation badges are rendered for ANY [N] the model emits (markdown-message.tsx regex /\[(\d+)\]/g), but handleCitationClick does sources?.[num-1] (positional). When Gemini hallucinates an out-of-range citation (e.g. [7] with only 3 sources) the badge is clickable but does nothing (silent dead click, no toast/error). When the model's [N] numbering does not match RRF source order, clicking [2] opens the WRONG source document. Both degrade trust in AI grounding.
repro_steps: 1) Seed workspace with 2-3 distinct notes/meetings so RAG returns 3 sources. 2) On /search ask a broad question; in the streamed answer find an inline [N]. 3) Click each [N] badge: verify each opens the SourceViewer panel for the correctly-numbered source (compare badge number vs the source list order in RagSources). 4) Specifically hunt for a [N] where N exceeds the source count (hallucinated citation): click it and observe no viewer opens and no user feedback. 5) Cross-check that the highlighted text in SourceViewer actually contains the claim.
expected: Every clickable [N] maps to a real source; out-of-range citations are either suppressed or give clear feedback; clicked source matches the cited number.
suspected_defect: Dead/no-op citation clicks for hallucinated [N]; mismatched source opens; user cannot verify grounding.
grounding: frontend/src/features/rag/components/markdown-message.tsx:22-40 (renders badge for any digit); rag-chat.tsx:55-69 handleCitationClick uses sources?.[num-1] with no bounds feedback; toHighlightChunk:25-32 always highlights full snippet (offset 0..len).

area: Invite max_uses exhaustion + expiry boundary (POST /invites, POST accept /invite/{code})
hypothesis: accept_invite deactivates the invite when use_count+1 >= max_uses, but the use_count increment and the _validate_invite check (use_count >= max_uses) are non-atomic across concurrent accepts. Two simultaneous accepts of a max_uses=1 invite could both pass _validate_invite (both see use_count=0) before either increments — potentially admitting 2 members on a single-use invite. Also verify expired invite (expires_at past) gives a clean isValid=false on /invite/{code} and 403/400 on accept, not a 500.
repro_steps: 1) owner d@e.com creates an invite with maxUses=1, expiresInDays=1. 2) Have TWO browser contexts (a@e.com + a fresh third account if available, else simulate via rapid double-submit) accept the SAME code near-simultaneously; check whether both become members (use_count over-run) or the second correctly gets 'used up'/already-member. 3) Create an invite, manually let it expire (or set short expiry) and verify /invite/{code} info shows isValid=false with Korean reason and accept returns InviteExpiredError (not 500). 4) Accept twice with the same account -> MemberAlreadyExistsError (409), not 500.
expected: Single-use invite admits at most one new member even under concurrency; expired/exhausted invites give clean validation errors; double-accept by same user is a clean 409.
suspected_defect: max_uses over-run under concurrency (2 members on max_uses=1), or 500/IntegrityError on race instead of graceful 409.
grounding: backend/src/workspaces/invite_service.py:159-210 accept_invite (_validate_invite check at :167 then increment at :198, deactivate at :201-202 — TOCTOU window); :284-293 _validate_invite checks use_count>=max_uses; add_member ON CONFLICT backstops duplicate same-user but not distinct concurrent users on max_uses=1.

area: Cross-workspace ProjectMember add (I-17) and personal-ws isolation (I-19) edge variants
hypothesis: add ProjectMember (require_admin) must reject adding a user who is NOT a WorkspaceMember of that ws (CrossWorkspaceMemberError 403) and reject add to personal ws (PersonalWorkspaceProtected). Edge variant: admin of team ws A tries to add a userId who is a member of ws B but not ws A -> must 403, not silently succeed. Also: can an admin add a ProjectMember to a DRAFT project (visibility=draft, creator-only) — does that leak draft access to a non-creator via ProjectMember, contradicting the draft 'creator-only, admin/owner do NOT bypass' invariant?
repro_steps: 1) owner d@e.com (ws A admin). Get a userId that exists in ws B but is not in ws A. POST /workspaces/A/projects/{P}/members with that userId -> expect 403 CrossWorkspaceMemberError. 2) In a personal workspace, attempt POST .../projects/{P}/members -> expect PersonalWorkspaceProtected. 3) Create a DRAFT project owned by a@e.com (member). As owner d@e.com (admin) add a THIRD user as ProjectMember of that draft project; then as that third user check GET /projects/{P} — does ProjectMember grant access to a draft project that should be creator-only? 4) Confirm I-17: add member with project_id from a different ws -> 404.
expected: Cross-ws user add -> 403; personal ws -> protected; ProjectMember should be meaningful only for private projects (draft is creator-only) — adding a member to a draft must not silently grant draft read access bypassing the creator-only rule.
suspected_defect: Cross-ws member admitted, or ProjectMember on a draft project grants non-creator read access (visibility invariant inconsistency between draft and private).
grounding: backend/src/projects/service.py:182-224 add_member (CrossWorkspaceMemberError at :206, personal block :202); router.py:133-147 require_admin; _visibility_filter_sql:166-183 private uses ProjectMember but draft uses created_by_id only — adding ProjectMember to a draft project has no effect on draft access path, worth confirming UI doesn't imply otherwise.

area: Onboarding 0->4 live signup + step gating (GET /users/me/onboarding, OnboardingBanner)
hypothesis: Onboarding step advances are wired across separate hooks (lazy-seed step1 in get_current_user, project create step2, meeting distill step3, first RAG step4) but with a 60s User cache and graceful try/except that swallows failures. Risks: step does not advance because the increment is swallowed (warning-only) or stale due to invalidate_user_cache not being called; OnboardingBanner shows wrong step or never disappears at step4; a fresh signup hits a blank/broken dashboard before step1 seed completes.

Check OnboardingBanner shows step ~1. 3) Create first project -> banner advances to step2 (may lag up to 60s due to User cache — note the delay). 4) Distill a meeting/note -> step3. 5) Do first RAG ask on /search -> step4, banner should disappear. 6) At each step capture console for errors and confirm GET /users/me/onboarding step matches UI.

area: Export UTF-8 filename + content integrity (GET /notes/{id}/export, /meetings/{id}/export)
hypothesis: Export sets Content-Disposition: attachment; filename*=UTF-8''<quoted title>. Edge: a note/meeting title containing Korean, emoji, slashes, quotes, or newlines may produce a broken/garbled downloaded filename or a header-injection-shaped value. Also MD export embeds title and plain_text without escaping — a title with markdown/control chars could corrupt the .md; JSON export uses ensure_ascii=false so must remain valid UTF-8.

area: RAG /search — SemanticCache source_type filter bypass
hypothesis: find_similar_cache ignores source_type entirely; cache store is gated only by is_time_filtered. A cached answer/sources from a no-filter (or meeting-filtered) query gets returned to a query that explicitly filters sourceType=note (and vice versa), so the source-type filter is silently ignored on a cache hit. This is the exact analog of the time_range cache-skip fix (service.py:71) that was NOT applied to source_type.
repro_steps: As owner d@e.com: in the team workspace ensure both a meeting and a note exist and are embedded. Go to /search. Set 유형 = 모든 유형 and ask a distinctive question that both the note and meeting would answer (e.g. 'Sprint 15 wedge 결정'). Note the sources list (mix of note+meeting). Within 7 days (cache TTL) ask the SAME (or near-identical, >0.93 similar) question again but set 유형 = 노트. Observe the returned sources/answer.
expected: With 유형=노트, only note-sourced chunks should appear; meeting sources must be excluded. The answer should be regenerated against note-only context.
suspected_defect: Cache hit returns the previously cached answer + meeting+note sources despite 노트 filter; meeting content leaks into a note-scoped query and the source-type filter has no effect. done event shows cached:true.
grounding: backend/src/rag/service.py:71-80 (is_time_filtered gate, source_type NOT considered for cache) + :202-223 (save_cache gated only by is_time_filtered); backend/src/embeddings/repository.py:331-339 (find_similar_cache signature has no source_type param)

area: Inbox classify/confirm — '되돌리기' false-revert + persistence
hypothesis: handleConfirm persists the classify (classifyMutation sets is_processed=true on BE + invalidates cache), but the confirmed-state '되돌리기' button only does setStatus('idle') locally and never calls any un-classify/un-process API. So 되돌리기 is a false affordance: the item stays processed in the DB. After reload the item is gone from the unprocessed list regardless of revert.

area: Promote modal — 202 'in-progress' UX honesty (meeting/memory not RAG-searchable yet)
hypothesis: For meeting/memory/inbox/action the modal shows a success toast ('...을(를) 팀에 복사 중…') and closes immediately on 202, but embedding copy runs in a BG task (pending->processing->completed). Only note polls. So a user promotes a meeting to the team, the toast implies done, but the promoted item is NOT yet RAG-searchable in the target ws until the BG task finishes (and could end as 'failed' or 'n/a' with no UI signal).

Immediately switch to the target team ws as member a@e.com and run a /search RAG query that should match the promoted meeting. Re-run the query ~10-20s later. Compare results.
expected: Either the UI should communicate that embedding is still in progress (like the note polling path), or the promoted meeting should be searchable promptly; the user should not be misled that copy is fully complete.
suspected_defect: Toast says copy succeeded and modal closes, but the promoted meeting is absent from team RAG for the BG-task window; if the BG embed copy fails the audit goes 'failed' with zero user-facing feedback -> permanently unsearchable with no error shown.
grounding: frontend/src/components/shared/ItemPromoteModal.tsx:174-240 (only itemType==='note' polls embedding-status; others toast+close immediately) ; backend/src/meetings/service.py:411-425 (meeting promote schedules _bg_promote_embed_meeting, returns embedding_pending)

area: Note/Meeting export — filename from raw title (slash, empty, newline)
hypothesis: Export filename is built from the raw title: notes use `{title}.md` with 'Untitled' fallback, but meetings use `{meeting.title}.md` with NO empty fallback. A title containing '/' or control chars, or an empty meeting title, produces a broken/odd Content-Disposition. FE triggerDownload also builds `${noteTitle||'Untitled'}.${ext}` from the title independently. quote() encodes the whole filename including slashes so '/' becomes %2F (filename with literal %2F) rather than a clean name.
repro_steps: As owner d@e.com create a note titled 'A/B 결정: 요약\n2026' (include a forward slash and ideally a newline) with content, let it embed. Open the note, click 내보내기 -> Markdown and JSON. Inspect the downloaded filename. Repeat for a meeting: create a text-capture meeting with title '회의/긴급' and after completion export it. Also test a meeting whose title is empty/whitespace if creatable.
